steps.evidence: README.md:30 (npm run dev); CI uses npm run production (tests.yml:45); public/js and mix-manifest.json are gitignored
README.md:34 passes --db-name="akaunting" but never says to create it; Installer::createDbTables checks the DB is reachable first (app/Utilities/Installer.php:150)

README.md:34 (php artisan install --db-name=... --admin-email=... --admin-password=...); it moves .env.example to .env, sets APP_KEY, runs migrate + permissions seed, creates company and admin (Installer.php:135-166)

notes: README.md:30 writes 'composer install ; npm install ; npm run dev' on one line (split here); the git clone line is omitted. There is no separate env-copy or key:generate step: 'php artisan install' renames .env.example to .env and writes APP_KEY and DB_* itself. README's primary serving advice is a web server whose document root is the project root (README.md:39-41); 'php artisan serve' is offered as a quick alternative (README.md:43). README lists MariaDB/MySQL/PostgreSQL/SQLite, but .env.example uses DB_CONNECTION=mysql and the CLI installer only takes host/port/name/user/password, so MySQL/MariaDB is the practical default. Node must be 18-20 (README.md:18, engines '>=18 <21', advisory only via .npmrc engine-strict=false); node-sass ^9 needs a native build. CI runs tests only (cp .env.testing .env with SQLite in-memory, npm install, npm run production, composer test); its PHP matrix floor is 8.2. Full requirements live at akaunting.com/hc/docs (external, not read).
